Overview

Florence as a Business Centre

Florence is the capital of Tuscany and the centre of a metropolitan city of 41 municipalities with about 988,000 residents in 2026. Beyond tourism, which shapes much of the historic centre's economy, the area is a manufacturing and corporate base. A 2026 ranking of Florentine companies by revenue is led by Baker Hughes's Nuovo Pignone entities, which make turbines and compressors for the energy industry, followed by Guccio Gucci, the retail cooperative Unicoop Firenze, vehicle leasing, ICT distribution, Gucci's logistics arm, Salvatore Ferragamo and Eli Lilly's Italian subsidiary. Around these names sits a dense network of leather goods, footwear, textile and accessories workshops in the metropolitan area and the neighbouring Prato and Pisa provinces.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Florence largely because of supply chains. Luxury and fashion brands, and the investors and lenders behind them, need to know who actually produces their goods: Tuscan production often passes through layers of subcontractors, some of which have been investigated for labour exploitation. In January 2026 the Tribunale di Firenze placed the apparel company Piazza Italia under judicial administration over negligent facilitation of exploitation at Prato subcontractors, showing that brands, not only workshops, face consequences. Other work involves acquisitions of Tuscan family firms and hospitality assets, energy equipment partnerships, distributor and agent reviews, and disputes heard in Florence's courts.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Florence

01

Subcontractor mapping for luxury brands

Leather goods and apparel made around Florence can pass through several tiers of workshops. We map the companies behind a brand's suppliers and sub-suppliers, their owners, address and officer changes, prior proceedings and media, helping brands evidence the controls Italian courts now expect.

02

Labour exploitation risk indicators

Prosecutors in Tuscany have pursued exploitation offences in fashion supply chains. We look for public-record indicators such as short-lived companies, repeated phoenix successions at the same premises, prior labour inspections and related-party links, giving compliance teams a focused list for audits.

03

Acquisitions of Tuscan family firms

Investors buying Florentine manufacturers, hospitality businesses or brands review owners, family arrangements, related companies, litigation, tax disputes and reputation. We research Italian registry filings, court records and local press to surface issues that financial and legal diligence alone may miss.

04

Energy equipment partner diligence

Florence's energy engineering base works with customers and agents worldwide. We research foreign agents, distributors and counterparties for ownership, sanctions exposure, links to state officials and adverse media, supporting anti-corruption and export control programmes. Findings are sourced for the compliance file.

05

Counterfeit and grey-market networks

Florence's luxury brands and artisans are targets for counterfeit and diverted goods. We research the companies, online sellers and logistics links behind suspect products, supporting counsel deciding on civil action, customs measures or complaints to Italian authorities.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Florence

Tribunale di Firenze

The Tribunale di Firenze hears civil and commercial cases for the city, and its prevention section decides applications for measures such as judicial administration of companies under article 34 of the Anti-Mafia Code. Its January 2026 Piazza Italia decree was the first such measure for negligent facilitation of labour exploitation proposed by a district prosecutor. Company law and IP disputes go to a specialised business section.

Supply chain enforcement

Judicial administration does not require that the company itself committed a crime; it can follow from inadequate oversight of subcontractors under investigation for exploitation under article 603-bis of the Criminal Code. In the Piazza Italia case the court chose a supportive form that assists management rather than replacing it. For brands sourcing in Tuscany, documented supplier checks are now a practical legal safeguard.

Registries and chamber of commerce

Companies in the Florence area are registered in the Registro delle imprese kept by the Camera di Commercio di Firenze, part of the national business register, which provides officers, shareholders of limited companies, filed accounts and insolvency events. These records, combined with court information and local press, form the backbone of research on Florentine companies and their suppliers. Filings are in Italian throughout.

Licensed investigation in Florence

Private investigation in Italy requires a licence issued by the prefecture, as described on our Italy page. Where a Florence matter calls for local enquiries, TDSC coordinates investigators licensed by the competent prefecture and works through Italian counsel, who determines how findings may be used in civil, labour or criminal proceedings. Local enquiries are documented and limited to the stated purpose of the engagement.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Florence

TDSC has no office in Florence and works on Florence matters from Nashville. We start with the decision the work supports, whether a supplier audit plan, an acquisition, a partner appointment, a counterfeit response or a dispute, and agree its scope with the client's Italian counsel. Research uses the business register, filed accounts, published court decisions, press in Italian and English, and, for the Prato district, Chinese-language sources where relevant. Personal data is processed under the GDPR and Italian law with a documented purpose. Workshop visits or other local enquiries are carried out only by investigators holding a prefectural licence, coordinated through counsel and limited to what Italian law permits.

TDSC has no office in Florence. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Florence: Frequently Asked Questions

Why do luxury brands research their Florence suppliers?

Italian courts have placed fashion companies under judicial administration where they failed to supervise subcontractors under investigation for labour exploitation. In January 2026 the Tribunale di Firenze took that step against Piazza Italia. Mapping supplier ownership and risk indicators helps brands show proportionate oversight and decide where audits are needed.

Can you identify the owners of a Florentine company?

The Italian business register shows directors and, for limited companies, registered shareholders, as well as filed accounts and insolvency events. Where owners sit behind trust companies, holding entities or foreign vehicles, we research further records and media, and counsel advises on access to the beneficial ownership register, which has been subject to litigation.

Which courts decide commercial disputes in Florence?

Civil and commercial disputes are heard by the Tribunale di Firenze, with company law and intellectual property cases assigned to its specialised business section, and appeals to the Corte d'appello di Firenze. Contracts may instead select arbitration or another forum, which counsel takes into account when scoping research.

Do you research Chinese-owned workshops in the Prato area?

Yes, through Italian registry records, court and prosecution reports, local media and Chinese-language sources where available. We look for links between workshops, address and director changes and prior proceedings. Any on-site checks are scoped with counsel and carried out by licensed Italian investigators, never through pretexting.

Can TDSC run surveillance or workplace checks in Florence?

TDSC is not licensed in Italy and does not conduct surveillance itself. Italian law strictly limits monitoring of employees and the collection of personal data. Where enquiries are justified, we coordinate investigators licensed by the prefecture through the client's counsel and keep work within the defined purpose.
